newsitem.title: USA: US Fed's Phillips -- improved risk disclosure needed.
newsitem.headline: US Fed's Phillips -- improved risk disclosure needed.

text.p: Companies need to improve disclosure of risks, although there is not yet international consensus on the precise form added disclosures should take, Federal Reserve Governor Susan Phillips said Thursday.

"Individual firms should pursue better ways to disclose the nature and magnitude of the risks they assume, and their earnings impact," she said in a speech to the University of Tennessee in Chattanooga released here.
She urged the Financial Accounting Standards Board to continue efforts to devise a "reasonable, consistent" framework for hedge accounting.

Central banks are considering implementing a new system as of the end of 1997 of regular reporting from the major dealers in the G-10 countries that would provide internationally consistent information on the size and structure of derivatives markets, Phillips said.
Two working groups the Fed launched in July are expected to issue supervisory guidance on audits and recommendations for improved public disclosure in 1997, she said.

A joint study by the Basle Committee and the International Organisation of Securities Commissions of derivatives disclosure by some of the largest banks and securities firms in the G-10 countries issued last year is being repeated and should be published by the end of this month, Phillips said.
Internationally, banking supervisors are giving increasing recognition to accounting and auditing standards, she said.

The Basle Committee plans to form a new Information Subgroup that will encourage adoption of better standards for public disclosure, both for trading and derivatives activities and for traditional balance sheet risk, she said.
Also the Basle Committee will form a new accounting task force to address ways of improving international accounting standards, Phillips said.
